principles: Criterion: PACKET's EXTRACT_PROMPT sentence, applied to the note text only. No item was dropped: every A-only and B-only item was judged to qualify (some unsure); items neither labeler listed were not added.

Same change, different quote (prose sentence vs commit line vs changeset title vs 'At a glance' bullet vs section heading): one item whose anchors list every verbatim span that states it. Commit lines, headings and glance bullets were added as anchors where the note repeats a labelled change.

Granularity: when one bullet, sentence, heading or commit line announces several changes (ZodMap min/max/nonempty/size; z.meta + z.describe; Hindi + Kannada; .validate + .validateAsync), the finer split is kept as separate items that share one group. Items quoted from different sentences are separate groups even under one heading. A shared anchor (e.g. a commit line naming three features) does not merge groups.

unsure is kept only when the note text cannot settle the criterion: opaque commit subjects ('Fix #5353', 'Improve tuple'), internal-sounding work with no stated user effect (opt-in 'ladder', util.cached, charCodeAt, compile indent), a dependency drop that may fall under the skip list, a frozen-exports side note, and the two extra cases of the 4.6 check-fold fix. A labeler's unsure flag is dropped when the change visibly alters error text, types, accepted input, emitted output, imports or performance of a public API.
Locale additions are new_api; locale message corrections are fix and qualify (they change the error text users see).

Performance commits qualify when they name a user-facing path or effect (validate, safeParse, compile, CommonJS require, bundle size, memory); implementation-only micro-optimisations are kept but unsure.

change_type: a new method or function (including on an existing class) is new_api; a new argument form or accepted input kind on an existing function is new_option; a corrected wrong result or wrong emitted schema is fix; a changed observable behaviour that was not wrong before (new distinct error, new emitted event, changed conversion) is behavior_change; a rename or no-longer-installed dependency is removal.

breaking (BREAKING_RUBRIC verbatim): removals, renames, no-longer-installed dependencies and raised minimums are breaking. A change is breaking when the note shows existing code now fails or behaves differently in a noticeable way, including validation that now accepts or rejects input it did not before (E.164, fromJSONSchema keywords, open-ended tuples, template-literal composition) and a changed runtime default (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS). Not breaking: corrections of wrong emitted output or wrongly reported values (JSON Schema fold, metadata getters), new optional features, and commit-line-only changes whose effect on existing code the note does not show (z.preprocess optionality).
